text:
Predicates:
Student(x) ::: x is a student.
WorksInLibrary(x) ::: x works in the library.
ComputerScience(x) ::: x is from the computer science department.
HasPartTimeJob(x) ::: x has a part-time job offered by the university.
TakesDatabaseCourse(x) ::: x takes the database course.
InstructedByDavid(x) ::: x is instructed by professor David.
WorksInLab(x) ::: x is working in the lab.
Premises:
∀x ((Student(x) ∧ WorksInLibrary(x)) → ¬ComputerScience(x)) ::: No students who work in the library are from the computer science department.
∀x (HasPartTimeJob(x) → WorksInLibrary(x)) ::: All students who have part-time jobs offered by the university are students who work in the library.
∀x (TakesDatabaseCourse(x) → ComputerScience(x)) ::: All students who take the database course are from the computer science department.
∀x (InstructedByDavid(x) → TakesDatabaseCourse(x)) ::: All students instructed by professor David are taking the database course.
∀x (WorksInLab(x) → InstructedByDavid(x)) ::: All students working in the lab are instructed by professor David.
Student(james) ∧ WorksInLab(james) ::: James is a student working in the lab.
¬HasPartTimeJob(jack) ∧ ¬WorksInLab(jack) ::: Jack neither has a part-time job offered by the university nor works in the lab.
Conclusion:
TakesDatabaseCourse(james) ⊕ HasPartTimeJob(james) ::: James either takes the database course or has a part-time job offered by the university.
